products.name: Databricks Data Intelligence Platform
products.description: Unified data lakehouse platform combining Delta Lake (open data format), Unity Catalog governance, SQL/Python/Scala/R notebooks, Lakeflow Designer visual ETL, Photon C++ vectorized engine, and integrated ML/AI workflows. IPO-bound market leader for ML-centric data engineering.
products.positioning: AI-first lakehouse for data engineers and ML teams; open Delta Lake + Spark-evolved compute; competing on unified ML/ELT capabilities and 20-40% cost advantage for ETL vs SQL-only warehouses.

products.name: Snowflake Cloud Data Warehouse
products.description: Enterprise cloud data warehouse with micro-partitioned columnar storage, virtual warehouse-based workload isolation, zero-copy data sharing, Iceberg write support, Cortex AI (Gemini 3.5 Flash multimodal), and advanced RBAC governance. Public company ($4.68B FY2026 revenue) dominating SQL-first analytics.
products.positioning: Enterprise SQL-first data warehouse; multi-cloud scale with workload isolation; competing on ease-of-use, performance for SQL analytics, zero-copy sharing, and mature governance.

products.name: ClickHouse Cloud
products.description: Real-time OLAP database combining column-oriented storage with sub-second aggregation performance. 10x faster join performance vs Spark/Snowflake. Managed Cloud service ($0.20/hr compute) + open-source self-hosted option. Targeting 250%+ YoY growth for fresh-data analytics and observability.
products.positioning: Real-time OLAP for high-ingest, sub-second analytics; cost leader via compression and open-source option; competing on speed, cost efficiency, and data freshness vs warehouse-evolved platforms.

products.name: Dremio Cloud Lakehouse Platform
products.description: Open lakehouse platform emphasizing vendor lock-in avoidance (Apache Iceberg/Parquet/Polaris Catalog). Intelligent Query Engine, Reflections acceleration, AI Agent with Mermaid visualization, multi-source federation. Recently acquired by SAP (May 2026, closing Q3 2026) for enterprise integration.
products.positioning: Open-lakehouse alternative to proprietary warehouses; no vendor lock-in via Iceberg/Polaris; competing on multi-source federation, agentic AI, and openness.

notes:
**EXTRACTION SUMMARY**

This Phase C extraction covers the primary data warehouse/lakehouse competitive landscape (4 products x 4 companies) relevant to MetroGraph's positioning as a visual graph tool for data exploration + workflow orchestration.

**Key Findings:**

1. **Market Consolidation**: Warehouse market dominated by scale (Snowflake $4.68B revenue) + momentum (Databricks $134B valuation, ClickHouse 3x YoY). Dremio acquired by SAP (May 2026), indicating ecosystem consolidation into enterprise ecosystems.

2. **HCI Failure Pattern** (MetroGraph's Wedge):
   - **Databricks**: Notebook UI collapse (scattered cells, sidebar complexity, no data relationship visualization)
   - **Snowflake**: SQL+config burden (users hide from cost complexity, relationships buried in JOINs)
   - **ClickHouse**: SQL-only workflow (no visual discovery of schema or pipeline freshness)
   - **Dremio**: Agent chat non-determinism (Mermaid diagrams help, but agentic reasoning adds uncertainty vs explicit graphs)

3. **Feature Differentiation**:
   - **AI/Copilot**: Databricks (full) = Snowflake (full) = Dremio (full) > ClickHouse (none). MetroGraph's edge: copilot + graph (not just code-gen).
   - **Data Sharing**: Snowflake (zero-copy native, A) >> Databricks (Delta Sharing, B) > Dremio (federation, B) > ClickHouse (none, F).
   - **Real-Time**: ClickHouse (sub-second, A) > Databricks (Photon, B) > Dremio (federation lag, B) > Snowflake (warehouse latency, C).
   - **Open Format**: Dremio (Iceberg-native, A) = ClickHouse (self-hosted, A) > Databricks (Delta-locked, B) > Snowflake (proprietary, C).
   - **Visual Exploration**: Dremio (semantic layer + agent, B) > Databricks (Discover page, B) > Snowflake (schema browser, B) > ClickHouse (CLI, C). **Gap: None excel at visual graph**. MetroGraph fills this.

4. **Threat Sequencing**:
   - **Databricks** (Threat: HIGH): Most directly competitive on workflows + AI. IPO imminent ($100B+ valuation) → likely to invest in UX.
   - **Snowflake** (Threat: HIGH): Enterprise gravity + cost surprise recovery. Cortex AI + Iceberg support closing lakehouse gap.
   - **ClickHouse** (Threat: HIGH): Fast-growing on real-time + cost. Limited for broad data discovery, but owns performance niche.
   - **Dremio** (Threat: MEDIUM): Weakened by SAP acquisition (integration risk), but open lakehouse + agent positioning relevant.

5. **MetroGraph Positioning**:
   - Wedge: Fix HCI failure of scattered, SQL-first, code-heavy platforms → visual graph UI for data exploration + workflow orchestration.
   - ICP: Data engineers + startups evaluating lakehouse/warehouse (Databricks, Dremio adjacency) OR cost-conscious teams (ClickHouse, Snowflake cost escape).
   - Differentiation: Only visual graph + node/edge model across all four. All competitors converging on AI copilot; MetroGraph differentiates on **UI + AI** parity (graph-aware copilot, not just code-gen).

**Sources Confidence**:
- Tier 0 (Official): 10 sources (docs, pricing, funding)
- Tier 1 (Release notes): 5 sources
- Tier 2 (Analyst): 10 sources (G2, Gartner, Forrester, TrustRadius)
- Tier 3 (Practitioner): 19 sources (comparisons, benchmarks, FinOps guides)
- **Total: 44 sources ingested**, covering official positioning, customer reviews, analyst reports, and practitioner insights.
